description: Log-normal distribution quantile function exp(mu + sigma Phi^-1(p))

tolerance.reason: The quantile is exp(y) with y = mu + sigma Phi^-1(p), so an absolute error in y is the relative error of the result. Rounding y costs |y| 2^-53, and a normal quantile q good to a few ulps (norm_ppf: within 2^-53 x 2.4 for statrs and SciPy) costs sigma |q| times that; |y| and sigma |q| are at most 152 and 154 on this grid (mu = 2, sigma = 4, p = 5e-324), so a careful method stays within about 6e-14. 1e-13 as for the other quantiles; results below 2.2e-308 are judged relative to that number (conventions)

grid: (mu, sigma) in {(0, 0.25), (-3, 0.5), (0, 1), (2, 4)} x the norm_ppf probabilities: p = 10^-k for k = 1..20 and 30..300 step 10, the doubles nearest 1 - 10^-k for k = 1..16, i/64 for i = 0..64, 1/2 +- 10^-k for k = 5, 10, 15, and 5e-324, 1e-310, 2^-1022; the quantile is 0 at p = 0 (the end of the support) and p = 1 is tagged pole (+inf)
